title: Energy-space Birkhoff normal forms for smoothing polynomial Hamiltonians with strongly nonresonant low-mode frequencies and multiplicities
source_title: Birkhoff normal forms for Hamiltonian PDEs in their energy space
author: Joackim Bernier; Benoît Grébert
difficulty_reason: Finite-dimensional formal homological elimination does not control an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian flow at energy regularity. Section3 proves harmonic-mean coefficient estimates and Poisson-bracket closure, including derivative bounds on both positive and negative Sobolev spaces. Section4 uses those new estimates in the degree-by-degree low-mode homological construction to obtain actual symplectic maps and a controlled remainder without demanding high-regularity initial data.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact abstract Theorem4.1: integer lattice subset, d>=1, s>=0, integers r>p>=3, quadratic frequencies bounded after weighting by <n>^-2s, generalized strong nonresonance Definition2.3 up to order r and cutoff Nmax, alpha>max(d-q,d/2), q>=0, d/2-q<s<alpha-d/2+q. Polynomial degrees p through r-1 have exact eta-scaled Hq,alpha coefficient bounds. Low super-actions group all equal frequencies; normal form and gradient remainder, near-identity symplectic inverse maps, cutoff-dependent radius and hs/h-minus-s derivative bounds retained. Complete new multilinear estimates, flow extensions, Poisson coefficient convolution, homological induction and remainder control30–47 plus Appendix7.1 convolution proof63 read. Existing Young/Hölder inequalities, Banach-space ODE uniqueness, duality and Gronwall are explicitly established foundations. The quadratic Hamiltonian in4.1 has its stated factor1/2, so its homological divisor is the printed single-frequency sum; the bound54 has an incidental factor1/2 and mismatched superscript constants, absorbed by the freely chosen positive constants. Initialization exponent j+2 instead of j-2, reversed comparison C-sharp<=1 on46 and suppressed absolute bars in Definition2.3 are unambiguously fixed by the immediately supplied assumptions and C-sharp=max(...,1) construction; no new normal-form argument is supplied. Does not include heuristic Theorem1.2, random-potential applications, or dynamical parameter variants. Author given name is Joackim as on the original PDF.
